chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Ya'qub: that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when he made a will,
some of his family said to him, 'You have willed away more than one-third.' He said, 'I have not, but what remains from my one-third is so-and-so, and it is for Muhammad ibn Isma'il.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams handle bequests exceeding one-third of the estate?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the practical application of the 'one-third' rule in Shia jurisprudence, clarifying that bequeathing more than one-third is permissible provided it is drawn from the heir's share rather than exceeding the total estate's third. The Imam’s precise calculation demonstrates the scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the fixed limit of one-third and the specific allocation of that portion, ensuring the testator's wishes are fulfilled without violating inheritance laws. This context highlights the flexibility within the Shia legal tradition regarding voluntary bequests (wasiyya) beyond the obligatory shares.
